extraction.name: FOMO60K
extraction.description: FOMO60K is a large-scale, heterogeneous dataset of 60,529 brain MRI scans from 13,900 sessions and 11,187 subjects, aggregated from 16 publicly available sources. It includes both clinical- and research-grade images, multiple MRI sequences, and a wide range of anatomical and pathological variability, including scans with large brain anomalies. It is intended to support the development and benchmarking of self-supervised learning methods in medical imaging at scale.
extraction.creator: Asbjørn Munk, Stefano Cerri, Jakob Ambsdorf, Julia Machnio, Sebastian Nørgaard Llambias, Vardan Nersesjan, Christian Hedeager Krag, Peirong Liu, Pablo Rocamora García, Mostafa Mehdipour Ghazi, Mikael Boesen, Michael Eriksen Benros, Juan Eugenio Iglesias, Mads Nielsen
extraction.rai:dataCollection: FOMO60K was aggregated from 16 publicly available brain MRI datasets. Minimal preprocessing was applied including reorienting images to RAS orientation, affine co-registration, and skull-stripping. The dataset includes both clinical- and research-grade images, multiple MRI sequences, and a wide range of anatomical and pathological variability.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Brain MRI scans from 16 publicly available sources including OASIS1, OASIS2, BraTS2024, MSD Braintumor, IXI, MGH Wild, NKI, and others. Scans include T1-weighted, T2-weighted, FLAIR, DWI, contrast-enhanced T1, Proton Density, SWI, and GRE sequences.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Existing neuroimaging resources are often curated for specific diseases or patient populations, and typically follow homogeneous imaging protocols with limited pathological variability. FOMO60K attempts to address this by including scans with large brain anomalies and capturing anatomical and pathological diversity.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Access to many existing neuroimaging datasets is restricted by formal applications, data use agreements, and institutional approvals, and data are commonly distributed in formats that require domain-specific preprocessing. FOMO60K is derived from 16 publicly available datasets but may still reflect the limitations of its source datasets.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: FOMO60K aims to democratize access to large-scale neuroimaging data for self-supervised learning research, lowering barriers to entry and enabling broader adoption of SSL methods in medical imaging.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains brain MRI scans, which are sensitive medical imaging data. Skull-stripping was applied to protect anonymization, and subjects have been shuffled to prevent easy identification of dataset sources.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for self-supervised pretraining and fine-tuning of models for medical imaging, as well as benchmarking and method development. It can be used with no further preprocessing for pre-training.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is publicly available on HuggingFace and will continue to grow in future releases as additional cohorts and modalities become available.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: MRI preprocessing comprised three main steps: reorienting images to RAS (Right–Anterior–Superior) orientation, affine co-registration, and skull-stripping. All scans were first reoriented to RAS and affinely co-registered using the mri_coreg command from FreeSurfer 7.4.1, with default parameters. Within each MRI session, scans were aligned to the image with the highest spatial resolution. For DWI scans stored in 4D format, b=0 volumes were extracted separately, and for the b=1000 shell, three diffusion-weighted volumes were selected based on gradient directions aligned with canonical x, y, and z axes and averaged to produce a single representative 3D image. Skull-stripping was performed using SynthSeg (FreeSurfer 7.4.1) when images were not already defaced or skull-stripped by the dataset provider, or when visual inspection identified residual cranial features.
